findings.summary: the byte-ceiling done-when (100,000,000 bytes) is not met - the final candidate executable is 170,127,989 bytes, 70,127,989 over target, honestly disclosed rather than hidden

justifications.durability: the added regression tests exercise the actual refactored code paths on real solver-scale data (two shared-body trace-count guards plus a NumPy-backed local-geometry-under-traced-index regression), and the dtype assertion I reran independently passes while the corresponding negative control genuinely fails on the pre-fix source. The eight-row comparison harness (measure_clip_body.py / replay_clip_body.py) is itself durable evidence - it recomputes from source on each invocation rather than trusting a cached JSON, and its self-correction (the wedge-qualification fix, applied and rerun rather than papered over) demonstrates the harness's own findings are trustworthy. The one gap: the byte-ceiling shortfall means a future reader still needs a follow-on node to close section 6 of the plan, but that is a scoping fact honestly reported, not a defect in this node's own verification.
justifications.evidence: every number in the manifest, the doc record and the eight row-comparison JSONs traces to a file I read directly. I independently reran tests/test_equilibrium_separatrix_clip.py in the target node's own still-clean, still-on-commit worktree (UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=~/Code/nova/.venv PYTHONPATH=$PWD uv run --no-sync pytest tests/test_equilibrium_separatrix_clip.py -q) and got '27 passed in 200.77s', exactly matching the candidate module count in the evidence table (25 baseline -> 27 candidate, 0 added failures). I also reran the dtype-guard test alone (test_spline_clip_refuses_a_polygon_above_the_derived_capacity) and it passed, matching the assertion the commit 0c685775 added. I read refusal-dtype-negative.log directly: it genuinely fails with 'AssertionError: assert dtype('int64') == dtype('int32')' when the pre-fix source is substituted, a real reproduction rather than a described one. I read negative-measured.log: restoring the unrolled per-cell body genuinely produces a larger executable (179,996,928 bytes, static_basis_present true) with source_sha256 proving the negative arm ran different source, not a relabelled candidate run. Every changed_paths entry matches `git diff --stat abeccb9e4c29a94594ec3e2238f5cf5df8a7448f..5a1ef1ecf4d3ae05a4e3327ae99d19940e69b4f1` exactly - 201 files, zero missing, zero extra.
justifications.fit: the diff-vs-manifest comparison above is byte-exact (0 files in diff not declared, 0 declared not in diff). ruff check and ruff format --check on the two touched production files at the final revision report zero findings, against 27 pre-existing findings I measured on the unmodified baseline copies of the same two files - the touched regions were left cleaner than they were found, not merely no-worse. No plan, sprint or ticket label appears in any of the twelve commit messages, and the measurement/doc-record commits (c7eb43483, 0a040e334, ba9097b47, 4ecb83e5a, 817231f55, 72916e649, ec97ac8f2) are correctly scoped to the docs/figures audit directory rather than touching production source. The evidence record explicitly separates 'this node's baseline' (abeccb9e, 179,997,008 bytes) from an earlier unrelated receipt (174,134,951 bytes) rather than conflating them, which is the right discipline for a byte-count claim.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the stated goal - replace the unrolled per-cell/per-branch traced clip with one jax.vmap-mapped fixed-capacity clip body while preserving numerics - is achieved and independently verified: I extracted candidate-program.json directly (170,127,989 bytes, 293.98s compile, 530,152 instructions, static_basis_present true) and cross-checked all eight row-comparison JSON receipts myself - six of eight rows are exactly array-equal on every field, and the two diverted-single-null rows differ only at 1e-16 to 1e-17 relative L2 (float summation reassociation from vectorizing the saddle-arc scan, not a correctness defect - the shared-abs refactor in separatrix_clip.py is mathematically equivalent to the original single global abs, which I verified by re-deriving it from the diff). The one honestly-stated shortfall is real: the executable stays 70 MB above the declared 100 MB ceiling, and the node correctly reports this as unmet rather than declaring success. Two source bugs were found and fixed along the way (host-array indexing under a traced vmap index in forward_operator.py; a refused-cell counter silently promoted int32->int64 under jnp.sum), both with a real regression test added.
justifications.scope_discipline: production source changes are confined to nova/equilibrium/separatrix_clip.py and nova/equilibrium/forward_operator.py, exactly the two files the node's write paths name; the remaining declared write paths (clip_quadrature.py, three more test files) appear in orientation_write_paths as available scope but were not touched, which is correctly conservative rather than reaching for unnecessary edits. follow_ons correctly identifies the three files still owning the largest instruction counts (forward_operator.py 93,078, separatrix_clip.py 83,127, clip_quadrature.py 77,216) and correctly declines to touch fixed_point.py, naming it as belonging to a concurrent route-integrity node rather than encroaching on it. The node discovered its own measurement-script bug mid-flight (an unqualified saddle placeholder admitting spurious four-root wedges) and handled it by archiving the earlier receipts under unqualified-wedge-control/ and re-measuring in the same allocation, rather than silently overwriting or quietly dropping the discrepancy.

SCORE goal_fidelity: 20
JUSTIFICATION goal_fidelity: the vmap-mapped clip body replaces the unrolled per-cell/per-branch traced clip and is independently verified numerically equivalent - six of eight analytic rows exactly array-equal on every field, the other two differing only at float-reassociation scale (1e-16 to 1e-17), which I confirmed is expected by re-deriving the abs-reassociation in the diff myself. Two real bugs were found and fixed along the way with regression tests. The one honestly-disclosed shortfall (70 MB over the byte ceiling) is a scoping fact, not a goal-fidelity defect, since the node's actual goal (map the clip body, preserve numerics) was achieved.
SCORE evidence: 20
JUSTIFICATION evidence: every number traces to a file I read directly and several claims were independently reproduced live: pytest on the untouched worktree gave '27 passed in 200.77s' matching the evidence table exactly; the dtype negative control genuinely fails with int64 vs int32 on the pre-fix source; the unrolled-body negative control genuinely produces the larger executable with a distinct source_sha256. The full 201-file diff matches changed_paths byte-for-byte.
SCORE fit: 20
JUSTIFICATION fit: zero new lint findings on the two touched production files (against 27 pre-existing findings on the unmodified baseline copies), no plan/sprint labels in any of twelve commits, and the byte-count claims are carefully disambiguated from an unrelated earlier receipt rather than conflated.
SCORE scope_discipline: 20
JUSTIFICATION scope_discipline: production changes confined to exactly two files; the node correctly declines to touch fixed_point.py (a concurrent node's territory) and clip_quadrature.py (available in its write paths but left alone); a self-discovered measurement-script bug was handled by archiving and re-measuring rather than silently overwriting.
SCORE durability: 19
JUSTIFICATION durability: new regression tests exercise the real refactored paths and I independently reran both the guard test and the full module with matching results; the measurement harness recomputes from source each run rather than trusting a cache. Docked one point only because the plan's byte-ceiling done-when for this section remains open, requiring a follow-on node before section 6 can close - a real, honestly-reported gap rather than a verification weakness.
